title.rendered: The Throne of Grace: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: The throne of grace — not the throne of performance review. Thursday’s devotional on Hebrews 4:16 and what it means to approach God with confidence rather than fear.

content.rendered:
The Gospel For Today | Thursday, April 30, 2026

📖 Today’s Scripture

“Let us then approach God’s throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.”
— Hebrews 4:16 (NIV) | ESV

📝 Today’s Message

Before the cross, the throne of God was a throne of judgment — approachable only by the high priest, only once a year, only with blood. Ordinary people could not come near. The veil kept them out. The distance was real, deliberate, and terrifying.

Then Jesus died. The veil tore from top to bottom, God’s doing, not man’s. And everything changed. The throne of judgment became the throne of grace. And the invitation was thrown open to everyone: let us approach with confidence.

The word translated “confidence” in Greek is parresia — boldness, freedom of speech, the right to speak openly without fear. It is the word used for the way a child runs to a father. Not tentatively. Not hoping they will be allowed in. With confidence because the relationship is secure and the welcome is guaranteed.

Religion teaches you to approach God carefully, guardedly, always uncertain whether you are welcome. The Gospel says: ” You are welcome. Jesus settled that question at the cross. Romans 5:1–2 says we have been given access into this grace in which we stand. The door is open. It has been open since Calvary.

Come boldly. Come freely. Come often. The mercy you need and the grace to help — they are already there, waiting at the throne, in your time of need.

🙏 Prayer

Father, I come boldly to Your throne of grace not because I have earned the right, but because Jesus paid for my access. I receive the mercy that covers every failure and the grace that meets every need. I refuse to stay at a distance that the cross already abolished. I come near, freely and confidently, as Your child. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

I have bold access to the throne of grace, not because of my performance but because of the blood of Jesus. The door is open and I am welcome. I approach with confidence today, not timidity. I receive mercy for every failure and grace for every need. The throne I approach is not a throne of judgment, it is a throne of grace, and I come freely, boldly, and without condemnation.
